meta.scope: Phase 14-09 substrate work — V40+V42+V43 migrations, session_termination, claudex_recall ID contract, generation-backend wrapper, CHR async, CLAUDE.md rules
meta.note: Averaged across 4 quality chunks. Higher = better except ai_generated_debt where higher = less AI-like debt.

findings.description: The Claude-default generation backend receives `model: model || 'sonnet'`, where callers pass `config.localModel` and the default config is an Ollama tag such as `glm-5.1:cloud`. Can make the Claude CLI receive an invalid model name.
`generate()` exposes `maxTokens` and `temperature`, but the Claude path drops them when calling `callClaudeSubprocessText`. Unified API does not honor its own contract consistently across backends.

Timeouts are not classified as transient because `isTransientError` checks 'etimedout' but `invokeClaudeOnce` returns stderr 'timeout'. Timeout failures throw after one attempt despite retry documentation.
`sweepChrQueue` is exported and tested, and the file header says retention GC calls it, but no production code imports it. Processed CHR rows accumulate.
Comment promises a `CLAUDEX_CHR_SYNC=1` synchronous classification path, but the code always enqueues.
`generateRich` returns `content: string | Record<string, unknown>` even when a schema is supplied. Ollama fallback schema parse failure silently returns raw text.
`enqueueChrClassification` catches all insert failures with no telemetry or error reason.
Phase-2 retry accounting keys on the first eight characters of the session id with a broad LIKE telemetry query. Can miscount on prefix collisions.
Prompt assets are manually duplicated into TypeScript strings with an instruction to paste updates in two places. High-maintenance drift risk.
`nowEpoch` stores `Date.now()` milliseconds for `valid_at_epoch_ms`. Name is misleading after the ms migration.

Decisions V17 view reads `$.timestamp_epoch_ms` but existing artifact JSON has `$.timestamp_epoch`. V43 renames relational columns only; existing V17-backed decisions return null timestamps and sort incorrectly.
Crash inference uses COALESCE over heartbeat, JSONL write, and creation time. Stale heartbeat + newer JSONL write incorrectly marks session as crashed.
V43 reverse migration guard checks `_ms` exists and legacy name is absent. Cannot distinguish freshly-created vs renamed columns; can rename canonical `_ms` columns on rollback.
V39-to-V40 is documented as epoch_ms canonicalization but also drops kind_registry legacy columns and rewrites `artifact_register_kind`. Unrelated cleanup increases blast radius.
`ArtifactLinkRow` still exposes `created_at_epoch`; schema and graph-walk now use `created_at_epoch_ms`, `valid_at_epoch_ms`, `invalid_at_epoch_ms`.
Health schema expectations require `artifact_links.created_at_epoch`; V43 renamed it to `created_at_epoch_ms`. V43 database falsely reported unhealthy.
Session termination writes return false on any failure without logging or telemetry.
Crash inference compares millisecond cutoff to last_heartbeat_ts/last_jsonl_write_ts, while existing hooks still write last_heartbeat_ts in seconds. Can back-fill active sessions as crash-terminated.
COALESCE checks last_heartbeat_ts before last_jsonl_write_ts; stale heartbeat can classify session as crashed even when JSONL activity is fresher.
Comment says CLAUDEX_CHR_SYNC=1 preserves synchronous classification; code never checks env var, always enqueues.
Ollama fallback passes opts.model literally. New callers pass Claude aliases like 'haiku'; CLAUDEX_GENERATION_BACKEND=ollama routes invalid Ollama model.
durationMs stores seconds after timestamp migration and is serialized as duration_s.
recordSessionTermination return value ignored in empty catch; failed termination writes are completely invisible.
artifact_id documented as 32-char hex V17 ID but validation accepts any non-empty string.
claudex_recent_sessions limit unclamped; negative or very large values produce unbounded SQL queries.
CLAUDE.md says V41 schema; src/core/migrations.ts exports TARGET_USER_VERSION = 43. Operationally risky for future schema/debug work.
Epoch rule says legacy `_epoch` columns still coexist until a future rename; migration layer already contains V43 rename-and-scale logic.
Audit presents '24 more legacy _epoch columns remain' as current state; V43 is already implemented. Needs timestamped/historical framing.
Audit headline says no unbounded external-IO awaits remain; same document later identifies filesystem awaits in user-profile-sync.ts without per-operation timeouts.
New rule is useful but prose is unusually long and emotionally phrased for an operational contract.
